html:
American woman who escaped slavery and went back many times to lead others to freedom. Born Araminta Ross into slavery in Maryland, she suffered a severe head wound as a girl when an overseer threw a heavy weight. It left her with spells and visions for the rest of her life.

In 1849 she escaped to Philadelphia. Over the next decade she made about thirteen trips back into Maryland and led some seventy people north, among them her family. She worked with the secret network of safe houses known as the Underground Railroad. People called her "Moses", and she later said she never lost a passenger.

In the Civil War she worked for the Union army as a cook, nurse, scout and spy. In 1863 she guided the Combahee River raid in South Carolina, which freed more than 700 enslaved people.

After the war she lived in Auburn, New York, cared for old and poor Black Americans and campaigned for women's right to vote. She knew Frederick Douglass and John Brown.
